builder_plan.scenario: A workflow needs specialist review, but extra agents may add more cost than useful work.
builder_plan.change: Test the proposed division of work against a single-agent implementation.
builder_plan.baseline: One agent with the same tools and an equal total token and time budget.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Accepted outputs, coordination failures, wall-clock time, and total cost across all agents.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: Proactive Agentic Orchestration
summary: POrchestra replaces static multi-agent orchestration, in which sub-agent goals and harnesses are fixed at creation, with sub-agents that can request runtime adjustments from the orchestrator; OPOD optionally replaces sparse-reward RL on the orchestration policy with process supervision distilled from hindsight revision requests. The cost is extra orchestrator-sub-agent communication rounds (added latency and tokens), plus training infrastructure for OPOD if the distillation component is adopted, though the runtime mechanism alone works with API models. It can fail when sub-agents issue unnecessary or poorly targeted revision requests, adding cost without quality gain, and the reported gains are benchmark averages that may not transfer to a different task mix or model family.
rationale: The runtime mechanism is adoptable with API models and public code, but the 9–10 point gains are benchmark-specific, so a small team should validate the orchestration overhead against their own workload before committing.
technique: Proactive sub-agent orchestration with policy distillation

claims.statement: POrchestra replaces static multi-agent orchestration, in which sub-agent goals and harnesses are fixed at creation, with sub-agents that can request runtime adjustments from the orchestrator; OPOD optionally replaces sparse-reward RL on the orchestration policy with process supervision distilled from hindsight revision requests. The cost is extra orchestrator-sub-agent communication rounds (added latency and tokens), plus training infrastructure for OPOD if the distillation component is adopted, though the runtime mechanism alone works with API models. It can fail when sub-agents issue unnecessary or poorly targeted revision requests, adding cost without quality gain, and the reported gains are benchmark averages that may not transfer to a different task mix or model family.

Improves task success by an average of 9.1 percentage points over the strongest baseline across three long-horizon agent benchmarks; combined with OPOD, improves small-orchestrator success by 10.0 points over existing training baselines, with a claimed better cost-performance trade-off.
